verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion capsule is scheduled to splash down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Floating in the Pacific Ocean on Friday... off San Diego" (R1); "splashed down in the Pacific Ocean, about 40 to 50 miles off the coast of San Diego" (R2); "splashdown about 50 miles off the coast of San Diego" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: All references directly confirm the splashdown location as Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion capsule is scheduled to splash down on Friday, April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Floating in the Pacific Ocean on Friday... April 10, 2026" (R1); "April 10, 2026" (R2); "Splashdown is targeted for 8:07 p.m. EDT... April 1" implying April 10 (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources specify Friday, April 10, 2026, as the splashdown date.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion capsule is scheduled to splash down at approximately 8:07 p.m. ET.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "splashdown, at 8:07 p.m. Eastern time" (R1); "The splashdown occurred at 8:07 p.m. ET" (R2); "Splashdown is targeted for 8:07 p.m. EDT" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Sources precisely state 8:07 p.m. ET/EDT as the scheduled splashdown time.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion capsule splashdown time of 8:07 p.m. ET corresponds to 5:07 p.m. PT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Splashdown is targeted for 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT)" (R4); "splashdown at 5:07 p.m. Friday" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: R4 directly equates 8:07 p.m. EDT (ET) to 5:07 p.m. PDT (PT); R8 confirms local time.

verifications.claim: The splashdown location is the Pacific Ocean approximately 40 to 70 miles west of San Diego.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "about 40 to 50 miles off the coast of San Diego... 40-50 miles southwest" (R2); "about 50 miles off the coast" (R3); "about 50 miles from San Diego" (R6); "50-70 miles right off of San Diego's coast" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Sources specify 40-50 or 50-70 miles off coast (southwest/west); claim's range and direction closely match.

verifications.claim: Recovery teams including the U.S. Navy and NASA personnel are positioned to retrieve the four-person crew.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "recovery team took more than an hour to approach... U.S.S. John P. Murtha" (R1); "U.S. military and NASA personnel are approaching Orion" (R2); "100 NASA and contractor personnel... United States Navy" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: All relevant sources confirm NASA and U.S. Navy recovery teams positioned for the four-person crew.

verifications.claim: The crew will be transported to the USS John P. Murtha.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "take them to the U.S.S. John P. Murtha" (R1); "flown to the flight deck of USS John P. Murtha" (R2); "fly them via helicopter to the USS John P. Murtha" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources explicitly state transport to USS John P. Murtha.

verifications.claim: The capsule will be inspected following the splashdown.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Once the capsule is pulled out of the water, “we’ll do some inspections”" (R1); "the capsule will be inspected and its valuable data retrieved" (R2)
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly state post-splashdown inspection of the capsule.

verifications.claim: The astronauts will be flown by helicopter to the U.S. Navy ship for medical checks before returning to shore.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "hoisted them up for hovering helicopters to take them to the U.S.S. John P. Murtha... medical bay for examinations" (R1); "hoisted into waiting helicopters and flown to... USS John P. Murtha... medical bay" (R2); "flown via helicopter to the USS John P. Murtha... post‑mission medical evaluations" (R4)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm helicopter transport to Navy ship (Murtha) for medical checks prior to shore return.
